criteria.criterion: `cargo test -p xtask` passes, including a new test that renders the real firstmate-work-handling study and asserts the glossary section and the `#next-steps` link both appear before the first transition card in the HTML.
criteria.evidence:
I ran it: all 4 tests in site_page passed. Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` also passed (1479 tests). `rendered_page()` runs the real binary (`CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask site --out `) and reads index.html. `check_order` requires `

Words used first

` and `` to come before the first `
`. It also requires that the next-steps and Glossary sections exist. In site.rs the full Glossary section comes after the cards by design (comment at line 447), and the out-of-scope list forbids layout changes. So the test reads the request's "glossary entry" as the word-defining start-terms block, which does sit before the cards. That reading is reasonable.

criteria.criterion: The new test asserts exactly which model-limit findings from studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json are present in the rendered HTML (and that others are absent), and `cargo test -p xtask` passes.
criteria.evidence:
`check_findings` takes the expected ids from findings.json, where kind == model-limit (f3 in the current data). Model-limit findings live in findings.json, not model.json, and the test reads the right file. It finds every `
  • ID what this page cannot show` in the 'Limits of this study' section. It reports any expected finding that is missing and any finding wrongly shown with that label. This matches site.rs lines 479-488 and kind_label. A guard fails the test if the study has no model-limit finding. The test passed.

criteria.criterion: The new test asserts that every transition whose model `trigger_evaluated_by` is `agent` is rendered as agent-decided, derived from model.json rather than hard-coded, and passes.
criteria.evidence: `check_evaluators` reads every transition and its `trigger_evaluated_by` from model.json. For each one it finds the card by `<h3>{id} <span class="arrow">` and requires `(decided by {by})` inside that card. That string matches site.rs line 388. It also fails if the model has no agent-decided transition. model.json has 7 agent and 4 code transitions. The test passed.

criteria.criterion: A committed fixture page (e.g. a deliberately wrong HTML file) is run through the same assertion helpers by a test that expects failure (glossary after first card, missing link, wrong findings, wrong evaluator), proving each check can fail; `cargo test -p xtask` passes.
criteria.evidence: xtask/tests/fixtures/bad_firstmate_page.html is committed. `the_wrong_fixture_page_fails_every_check` runs check_order, check_findings and check_evaluators on it and requires each of these exact problems: the word block comes after the card, the next-step link is missing, f3 is not rendered, f1 is rendered as a model limit, and t1 is not shown as decided by agent. The test passed.

summary:
The change does what was asked, and I'm passing it. The minor findings don't block it.

**What it adds:**
- **New test file:** `xtask/tests/site_page.rs` builds the real firstmate page by running the xtask `site` binary into a temporary directory, then checks three things:
  - The "Words used first" block and the `#next-steps` link come before the first transition card.
  - The findings shown as model limits are exactly the `model-limit` findings in `findings.json`.
  - Every transition card shows who decides its trigger, as `model.json` says in `trigger_evaluated_by`. The expected values are read from the data, not hard-coded.
- **Fixture that must fail:** a committed wrong page, `bad_firstmate_page.html`, is run through the same checks. A test requires each check to report its fault.
- **Convention text:**
  - One sentence in the change producer prompt.
  - A new doc, `docs/conventions/rendered-page-assertions.md`. I checked its claims against the code and they match.
  - A changelog entry and an update to `docs/design/requirements-map.md`.

All seven changed files are on the deliverables list. No reader, verifier or study prompt was touched. The only change to `site.rs` is a comment, so the page renders the same as before.

**Results:** I ran `cargo test -p xtask --test site_page` and all 4 tests passed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs also passed.

**Minor finding:** criterion 1 says "glossary section", but the test checks the "Words used first" block. The full Glossary section still comes after the cards, as the site code intends. Since the request says "glossary entry" and forbids layout changes, this reading is defensible.
